main_text.l: Clarissimo viro D. IOHANNI DRVSIO, Juper curis ejus Historicis.

QUicunque Sacrae praestitem Scientiae Olim audiisti Drusium; Quicunque linguas pluribus non cognitas Docente discis Drusio; Qua voce jura dixerit Deus sua Seris Isaci posteris; Quibusque verbis invias rerum vias, Et si quid oculis abditum est, Alumna VERI, prisca doctrinae parens Chaldaea gens descripserit; Huc, huc adesto. Divus, en, Divus Senex Meliora mentis pignora Sacrabit ævo, quae nec Invidentia, Nec Momus ipse lancinet. Ille, ille partis sat beatus laudibus, Privaque claritudine Non ante curis terminum tamen suis Metamque ponit ausubus,

page.notes: The first word of the poem has a large initial Q; I read the next letter as V, a vowel, so I wrote it as U. The heading's first word "Clarissimo" is set in italic with a mark over "viro" that I could not read clearly. "Juper" in the italic heading is printed with a letter that could be S; I copied it as printed. "iura" in line 3 is printed "jura" and I kept the letter as printed. The sign and italic in the heading are not confirmed letter by letter. The catchword "Quàm" is at the lower right, below the last line.
